response.answer: I can’t advise whether the clinician should increase the dose. The record shows the administrative request N-101 remains open because the signed office note and signature page are missing; dosing decisions are clinical and must be made by the treating clinician or pharmacist. If the clinician chooses to change the dose, the office should have the clinician sign the note and submit the complete signed note and signature page through the established secure channel, referencing ALD-1042 and request N-101. If the office needs to confirm acceptable signature formats or alternatives, that question should be sent to the receiving team for their determination.

passages.title: ALD-1042 · Recorded case briefing
passages.text: Avery Chen’s administrative objective is to help the office supply the item requested in N-101 and obtain a clear receiving-team record. The immediate blocker is the missing signed office note and signature page. An unsigned note already in the package does not satisfy the request. The next useful office discussion should confirm how to provide the complete signed note through the established secure channel, without asking Avery to validate clinical content.

passages.title: Office-note troubleshooting playbook
passages.section: Only an unsigned copy is available
passages.text: If the office has only an unsigned copy, clarify that the open request is for the signed note and its signature page. Ask the office to coordinate with its authorized clinician or documentation staff. Do not ask support staff to sign for the clinician, paste a signature onto the note or alter clinical content. If the office cannot obtain the requested document, route that limitation to the receiving team for an explicit next step.

passages.title: Documentation ownership and handoff worksheet
passages.section: An escalation request that can be acted on
passages.text: A useful request to the receiving team asks a precise question: clarify the document requested, locate a reported submission, identify a missing page, or confirm whether a received note satisfies the administrative request. Supply relevant case and transmission references through the secure support process. Ask for the team’s finding and the next administrative step. Do not include a speculative payer outcome, a fabricated service-level deadline or an unsupported clinical justification.

passages.text: Useful questions for the next Alder office conversation are: Can the office obtain the complete signed note and signature page? Is any part of the request unclear? passages.title: Missing-document follow-up guide
passages.text: Ask the office to provide the complete signed note through its established secure document channel and reference case ALD-1042 and request N-101. The Knowledge Pack does not contain an actual upload URL, fax number or secure-channel address. Do not place patient records in an ordinary email.

passages.title: Office correspondence examples
passages.text: Example clarification draft, not sent: “We want to make sure the correct document reaches the team. Could you confirm whether N-101 requires the complete signed office note and its signature page, and advise how to resolve any remaining document discrepancy?” Keep the message focused on the document question. Avoid accusing the office of failing to respond, adding a due date absent from the request, or asking for unrelated clinical records.

passages.title: Signed-note preparation checklist
passages.text: The Alder pack requests a signed office note including its signature page, but it does not define accepted electronic-signature formats, countersignature rules or who may sign on a clinician’s behalf. Those questions require clarification from the receiving team and the office’s authorized staff. A typed name or an unsigned copy must not be treated as accepted solely because it is readable. Pathway cannot authenticate a signature or decide whether clinical documentation is sufficient.
